title: Docker
summary: Docker builds images from a Dockerfile and runs services from a Compose file, with context, cache, tag and merge rules an agent must respect.

sections.label: Where config lives
sections.text: Docker reads a file named Dockerfile at the root of the build context unless the build names another file. A .dockerignore in the context root excludes matching context files, and a Dockerfile specific ignore file takes precedence when present. Compose supports compose.yaml, compose.yml, docker-compose.yaml and docker-compose.yml, preferring compose.yaml. Without an explicit file selection, it searches the working directory and its parents. docker init scaffolds .dockerignore, Dockerfile, compose.yaml and README.Docker.md and offers to overwrite existing files.

sections.label: Conventional commands
sections.text:
# Conventions, not facts about any project. Check its own scripts first.
docker build -t myapp:dev .
docker build --check .
docker compose up --build
docker compose down

sections.label: How CI is declared
sections.text: Docker does not declare a pipeline. Its CI pages present the Dockerfile as a way to define the runtime, operating system and binaries needed to build and test the application in a reproducible container. Docker maintains official GitHub Actions for building, annotating and pushing images and links setup for GitLab, CircleCI and Render.

sections.label: Where review conventions live
sections.text: Build checks inspect the Dockerfile and build options for deviations from current best practices without running the build, and docker build --check reports violations with a non zero exit status. In a regular build, check violations are warnings by default. To make that build fail on them, use # check=error=true or the corresponding BUILDKIT_DOCKERFILE_CHECK argument. The separate --check command already exits with a non zero status on violations. Checks need Buildx 0.15.0 and Dockerfile 1.8 or later. Other rules are the project's own.

sections.label: Gotchas
items: A filesystem context makes its files available to COPY and ADD after ignore rules. Files are loaded as needed, rather than necessarily all copied into the image. Exclude unnecessary local directories such as node_modules and .git. Git contexts omit .git by default unless configured otherwise.
When a layer changes, downstream layers in that build chain need rebuilding. Copy package manifests and install dependencies before frequently changing source to preserve useful cache entries.
An image reference without an explicit tag or digest defaults to latest. Tags are mutable, while a pinned digest does not pick up fixes until it is updated.
USER sets the user for later RUN steps, ENTRYPOINT and CMD, and Docker recommends a non root user when the service can run without privileges.

By default Compose merges compose.yaml with an optional compose.override.yaml. Explicit -f files are applied in order. Later values can replace or append according to each field's merge rule, so inspect the merged configuration rather than assuming a whole file wins.
The top level version key in a Compose file is obsolete and not used for validation.
Multi stage builds let you copy selected artifacts into a final stage without its build tools. This depends on the Dockerfile contents. docker build --target selects a named target stage.

sections.label: What Atlas provides
sections.text: Selecting Docker adds the Containerised services profile, which asks about the files a change touches, image pinning, build checks and the runtime user, and does not install Docker, build or verify an image.

sections.label: Check in your environment
sections.text: Confirm the installed Docker and Compose versions, which Compose files and overrides exist, whether build checks run, and whether a project script wraps these conventional commands.

sections.label: Review scope
sections.text: Scoped claims checked on 2026-10-12 against current Docker Build, Dockerfile, Buildx and Compose documentation. Build checks require the stated versions. CLI examples are conventions, not observed builds or verified runtime behavior.

basis: Scoped official documentation and proposed project guidance
confidence: The listed factual claims were checked against their sources on 2026-10-12 within the stated version and host scope. Recommendations and example commands do not prove suitability or execution in a particular project.

catalog.applicability: Use when a project builds container images from a Dockerfile or runs services with Docker Compose and a coding agent must build, run or review those files.
catalog.limits: Catalogue inclusion does not install Docker, verify a build, or confirm image contents, registry access or runtime behaviour.
